mathematical_result.name: QFORM-COLLINEAR-MINORITY-TWO-HEAVY-REARRANGEMENT-v1
mathematical_result.scope: Explicit exact-rank-three source-valid frames with two diffuse majority-sign banks and two arbitrary cap-one heavy physical laws loaded collinearly on the minority-sign axis; theorem is for the Gaussian-completion limit and all output locations.
mathematical_result.statement: For W=G1^2+G2^2-6(X+Y)^2 with G1,G2 iid standard Gaussian independent of arbitrary independent cap-one X,Y, ||p_W||_infinity <= B0=int_0^1(1-u)e^{-3u^2}du. Equality holds for centered unit intervals at output zero. Hence the physical Q limit has exact sharp branch constant C_col=12B0=2sqrt(3pi)erf(sqrt3)-2+2e^{-3}=4.1516968595129935..., strictly below 3sqrt2 by 0.090943827606292....
mathematical_result.mechanism: Bathtub/extreme-point reduction of the two cap-one laws to unit-measure sets, followed by one-dimensional Riesz rearrangement. For negative output t=-6a^2 the two-shell kernel has exact symmetric decreasing rearrangement (1/2)exp(-3u^2-6a|u|).
mathematical_result.finite_source_family: R_m rows: m copies e1/sqrt(m), m copies e2/sqrt(m), two copies e3/sqrt(2); R_m^T R_m=I3 and A_m=R_m diag(1,1,-1)R_m^T has nonzero spectrum {1,1,-1}.

partner_result_applied.use: Weak lower semicontinuity of interval concentration shows the centered-interval branch limit is approximated from below by finite source-valid matrices; invertible-matrix equivalence prevents dismissing lower-bound stress solely because the displayed frame is rank three.

unresolved_implication: The full QFORM theorem remains open. A sharper witness must leave this branch, e.g. genuinely non-collinear multi-direction heavy rows, unsaturated leverage plus residual Gaussian noise, three or more heavy rows, finite/mesoscopic overshoot, additional spectral directions, or another coupled off-zero geometry.
next_step: Attack a genuinely non-collinear opposite-sign two-heavy frame with the output-integrated rearrangement/half-Riesz weight retained; do not revive the corrected-false pointwise radial Gaussian-Laplace domination.
